goal: Replace literal-user confirmation of native Review verdicts with automatic reviewer authority derived only from a manager-owned terminal handle bound to the exact operation and task snapshot, while shared events and model output remain inert.

acceptance.assertion: The consumer requires the exact pre-installed direct manager terminal-port protocol and provider identity, captures one immutable terminal Promise at spawn, and never derives spawn or terminal authority from shared extension events or mutable AgentRecord fields.

One opaque single-use host receipt binds the exact task, native agent, local operation, assurance snapshot, terminal result digest, successful status, and provider protocol before reviewer verdict parsing or capability minting.

A receipt-bound Review pass records exactly one fresh reviewer approval, while receipt-bound rework records bounded findings and returns the task to working, with neither outcome opening ctx.ui.confirm.

Forged or replayed events, wrong task or agent or operation, malformed and prompt-injected output, stale snapshot or result, provider downgrade, duplicate settlement, cancellation, timeout, shutdown, and late completion perform zero unauthorized TaskRecord writes.

record-review-verdict is absent from routine Agent and slash-command authorization surfaces, genuinely privileged confirmations remain unchanged, Rule 1437 documentation reflects host-attested automatic Review authority, and the complete repository suite passes.
The provider enrollment gate and temporary fork exit milestone are documented, historical TaskIntent and TaskRecord data remain readable without migration, and the complete repository suite passes.
